actually decides). Both were written from one spec, both were
tested, and they disagreed about the value 0 for months: Swift read
JSON 0 as a boolean (NSNumber bridges to Bool) and refused it, so
the first page of every paged fs.read failed and WhatsApp export
ingestion read zero bytes. Neither suite noticed, because each
So the examples live HERE, once, and both suites iterate this file:
Adding a case is a deliberate act that both sides must satisfy.
'verdict' is what BOTH validators must do. 'why' is for the human.

Non-ASCII values are written as \uXXXX escapes on purpose: this file's whole job is to make a boundary value readable, and 'caf\u00e9' versus 'cafe\u0301' are indistinguishable as raw bytes in a diff.

cases.why: zero is a non-negative integer; it is the FIRST page of every paged read
one is an integer, not JSON true
the other value NSNumber-to-Bool bridging swallows
the default page size: the second page's offset
the executor's read ceiling, exactly
negative offsets have no meaning and must not wrap
one JSON number has several exact values, so it cannot be canonically signed
a real boolean is not an integer, and must not be read as 1
a numeric string is not an integer; no coercion anywhere in this path
a forbidden key name; the model cannot grant itself anything by argument
paths are absolute; a relative path resolves against an unknown cwd
secret-bearing names are outside every verb's reach, on both lanes
path is required
the ordinary case, so an over-strict rule fails here too
a bare capability name is the only shape an enum argument may take
an enum argument must never carry a path, or the probe becomes an oracle for walking the filesystem
traversal in an enum argument
the empty name is not a member of the closed set
body.probe has no path argument at all; adding one must be refused, not ignored
the ordinary write: a payload is a string and this one is already NFC
an empty payload truncates a file; it is a legitimate write, not a missing argument
a composed payload passes: NFC is what ACE hashes and what lands on disk
a DECOMPOSED payload: ACE would sign its composed form, so the bytes written would not be the bytes sent. Refused, never normalised for the caller
a number is not a payload; what bytes reach the disk must not be a coercion decision
nor is a boolean, and JSON true must not become the four bytes 'true'
the secret-name gate governs writes exactly as it governs reads: policy, not a permission
path is required; a write with no target is not a smaller write
a decomposed `old` would be signed composed and then match nothing on disk: the silent-zero-occurrences bug, refused at the gate instead
fs.edit requires all three: an edit with no replacement is a deletion nobody approved
the minimum: command and cwd, no timeout_ms (the executor's own ceiling applies)
cwd is REQUIRED: it is the jail's one writable subtree, so it is a security-relevant display line and there is no honest default (the executor's home is /var/empty)
timeout_ms is an integer; the executor clamps it to its own ceiling and says so in the result
zero on an intKey OTHER than fs.read's offset: the NSNumber-bridges-to-Bool trap is per-value, not per-verb
a decimal STRING is not an integer; untyped it would canonicalise, be signed, and then be ignored by whatever reads it
negative is not a duration
a JSON boolean must never be read as 1: true and 1 are the same NSNumber shape and only the ObjC type encoding tells them apart
an unclassified argument is a STRING. A number renders as 'command: 5' on the sheet, takes TWO fingerprints, then fails at dispatch as 'missing command'
same rule for a boolean: the command is executed byte for byte, so its type is the thing being approved
cwd is a path and must be absolute
cwd is root-checked like every other path: outside every compiled root, and widening a root is a code change and a re-sign
a lexical climb out of the roots resolves to /etc; the cwd is the jail's writable subtree, so this is the sharpest path in the catalogue
deny-by-name applies to cwd too: the jail also denies ~/.ssh, but the gate must refuse before the jail is ever asked
the schema is closed: an unknown key is refused, never ignored
